intent: Bring the last three unformatted markdown files under prettier, cap the billsplit Android build's memory so it cannot exhaust a 7.6 GB machine, and repair an e-paragon parser test that a previous prettier pass silently broke.
scope: billsplit/android/gradle.properties — JVM and daemon memory ceilings
billsplit/test/fixtures/sample_receipt.json — restored to its original minified bytes
billsplit/test/eparagon_parser_test.dart — regex hardened against JSON whitespace
Non-goal: making billsplit build an Android APK; that is blocked upstream by file_picker and is not attempted here
Non-goal: any change to billsplit's Dart behaviour or the app's dependency set
changes: Formatted the three remaining unformatted markdown files. The edits are cosmetic and markdown-correct: escaping `L*` to `L\*` so it stops rendering as emphasis, normalising `*em*` to `_em_`, and aligning tables.

Lowered billsplit/android/gradle.properties from the Flutter template's `-Xmx8G -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=4G` to `768m/512m`, and cut the number of JVMs with kotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process, org.gradle.daemon=false, org.gradle.parallel=false and org.gradle.workers.max=1. The template default asks for more than this machine has.

Fixed a regression I introduced and had already pushed: an earlier prettier pass pretty-printed billsplit/test/fixtures/sample_receipt.json, and the test `accepts bare JPK payload and bare JWS token` reads that file as RAW TEXT with a regex matching `"data":"..."` with no space after the colon. Pretty-printing inserted a space, the match returned null, and the null-check operator threw. My earlier check compared the PARSED JSON for equality, which passed and proved nothing about the raw-text contract.
Restored the fixture to its original minified bytes — verified byte-identical to the pre-formatting version — because it is a captured real e-paragon and a real one arrives as single-line JSON.
Added billsplit/test/fixtures/ to .prettierignore so captured payloads stay byte-faithful and this cannot recur by the same route.

Hardened the test regex to `\"data\"\\s*:\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"` and added an explicit isNotNull assertion with a reason, so a whitespace change now fails with a readable message instead of a bare null-check crash.

verification.evidence: 59 passed. Before the fix this run failed with 'Null check operator used on a null value' at eparagon_parser_test.dart:67.

verification.command: Generalisation check — temporarily pretty-print the fixture and re-run the repaired test, then restore
verification.evidence: The test passes against BOTH the minified fixture and the pretty-printed form that originally broke it, so the fix is not specific to the one byte layout. Fixture confirmed byte-identical to the original afterwards.

verification.command: prettier --check over all 525 tracked md/json/yaml files
verification.evidence: 'All matched files use Prettier code style!' The fixture is now reported as excluded rather than checked.

verification.command: pre-commit run --files $(git diff --cached --name-only), inside systemd-run MemoryMax=2G MemorySwapMax=0
verification.evidence: Every hook passes with no bypass, inside a hard 2G cgroup.

risks: billsplit still cannot build an Android APK: file_picker 11.0.3 (the latest on pub.dev) puts the Kotlin Gradle Plugin on the global classpath via rootProject.allprojects, which AGP 9 rejects, while turning built-in Kotlin off leaves file_picker's own Kotlin uncompiled. The launcher icon is therefore verified only by the preview sheet and a resource-resolution check, never by a build.

The gradle.properties ceilings were exercised through a full compileDebugJavaWithJavac but never through a complete successful assembleDebug, because the build fails upstream of packaging for the reason above.
Peak PSS observed during those Android builds was 2.03 GiB and 3.01 GiB — above the 2 GB budget for this machine. Nothing was OOM-killed, but an Android build here is not yet inside budget.
The .prettierignore entry covers billsplit/test/fixtures/ only. Another app adding captured payloads elsewhere gets no such protection and can hit the identical trap.
rollback: git revert the commit. The markdown edits and .prettierignore entry are inert; reverting gradle.properties restores the 8G template default, which is what endangered the machine, so prefer keeping that hunk.
After rollback, re-run flutter test in billsplit: the fixture and the regex must move together, since the old brittle regex only works against the minified fixture.
